cards.text: Friend, Paul the apostle wrote this letter to the believers in Rome (Romans 1:1, 7), and he's coming down the home stretch. He's taught them a LOT, and now he tells them he's convinced they're full of goodness and brimming with knowledge. Now, when somebody tells you you're GREAT, you start bracing for the "but"... and I'm already bracing.

cards.question: Paul says the believers in Rome are full of goodness and brimming with knowledge. What else does he say they're able to do?

cards.text: And there it is, friend. There's the however! Paul says he has written to them boldly on some points.

cards.question: Paul knows the believers in Rome are already full of knowledge. So he calls what he's written them a bold ___ on some points.
Paul is writing boldly to believers who already know a lot. Why does he say he can?

answers.text: Because of the grace God has given him
Because the church in Rome asked him to
Because he started the church in Rome

cards.text: That grace gave Paul a job: to be a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles. And he describes that job like a priest's work, the priestly service of the gospel of God.

cards.question: Paul's work is priestly service. He does it so the Gentiles might become an ___ acceptable to God.
Paul says the Gentiles who become an offering to God are made holy by the Holy Spirit.

cards.text: So Paul says he exults in Christ Jesus in his service to God. Friend, the man is THRILLED about this work.

cards.question: Paul is thrilled about his work among the Gentiles. When he talks about it, what does he say he'll speak about?

answers.text: Only what Christ accomplished through him
Only what he did in his own strength
Only what the other apostles have done

cards.text: If all that got done through ME, I'd have it stitched on my apron in CAPITAL letters, with sprinkles. Paul just points back to Christ, who led the Gentiles to obedience through him by word and deed, by signs and wonders, and by the power of the Spirit of God.

cards.question: Paul says he has fully proclaimed the gospel of Christ from Jerusalem all the way around to ___.

cards.text: Now Paul tells them how he picks where to go. He's got a goal for every new place he preaches.

cards.question: What's Paul's goal for where he preaches the gospel?

answers.text: Where the churches were already strong

cards.question: Paul wants to build on a foundation someone else has already laid.

cards.text: Some folks buy the house that's already built, but Paul is out there shopping for EMPTY LOTS. And he backs up his plan with Scripture, from Isaiah 52:15.

cards.question: Paul quotes Scripture to back up his plan. It says those who were never told about Him will never see.

cards.text: Now Paul turns to his travel plans. All that preaching where Christ wasn't known? He says that's why he's often been kept from coming to Rome.

cards.question: Paul says there are still plenty of opportunities left for him in the regions where he's been preaching.

cards.text: No more opportunities there, and Paul has longed to visit them for many YEARS. That's the group chat that's been saying "we HAVE to get together" since forever, and somebody finally starts making a plan.

cards.question: Paul is finally planning his visit to the believers in Rome. He hopes to see them on his way to where?
After enjoying their company for a while, Paul hopes the believers in Rome will help equip him for his journey to Spain.

cards.text: But not yet. First Paul is on his way to Jerusalem, the classic "I'll be RIGHT there, I just gotta make one stop."

cards.question: Paul says he's on his way to Jerusalem to ___ the saints there.

cards.text: Here's what that stop is about. Macedonia and Achaia were pleased to make a contribution.

cards.question: Macedonia and Achaia were pleased to make a contribution. Who is it for?

answers.text: The poor among the saints in Jerusalem
The leaders of the church in Rome

cards.text: They were pleased to give, and Paul says they owe it to them too. Friend, that's the rarest thing in the world: somebody who's GLAD to pay what they owe.

cards.question: Paul says the Gentiles owe the saints in Jerusalem. Why?

answers.text: They shared in their spiritual blessings
Jerusalem once paid for their churches
Jerusalem sent Paul to them first

cards.question: Paul says the Gentiles should pay Jerusalem back with spiritual blessings.

cards.text: So here's the plan: safely deliver the gift to Jerusalem, then set off for Spain by way of Rome. Jerusalem, Rome, SPAIN, friend, Paul's not planning a trip, he's planning a whole season.

cards.question: Paul knows that when he comes to Rome, he will come in the fullness of the ___ of Christ.

cards.text: Then Paul asks them for something. He urges them, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Spirit, to join him in his struggle.

cards.question: Paul urges the believers in Rome to join him in his struggle. How?

answers.text: By praying to God for him
By sailing to Jerusalem with him
By sending him money for Spain

cards.text: And Paul doesn't leave it vague. He hands them the prayer list.

cards.question: Paul asks them to pray that he's delivered from the ___ in Judea, and that his service in Jerusalem is ___ to the saints there.

cards.text: All so that, by God's will, he can come to them with joy and be refreshed together with them. Then he closes this part with a blessing: "The God of peace be with all of you. Amen."

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 3 quotes "we HAVE to get together", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "And there it is, friend." / "There's the however!" / "Paul says he has written to them boldly on some points." It isn't the opening card, so it can have only 1 to 2.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The setup gives a reason the text doesn't give: "Paul knows the believers in Rome are already full of knowledge. So he calls what he's written them a bold ___." Romans 15:14-15 puts the two side by side with "However." The only reason the text gives for writing is "because of the grace God has given me."

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: "He's got a goal for every new place he preaches" points toward the next card's right answer, "Where Christ was not known." It also rules out "Where the churches were already strong." Romans 15:20 never says "new place."

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "Now Paul turns to his travel plans." / "All that preaching where Christ wasn't known?" / "He says that's why he's often been kept from coming to Rome." It isn't the passage's opening card, so the limit is 2.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Macedonia and Achaia show up here as the givers, but the card never says who they are, such as the believers in Macedonia and Achaia, regions of Greece. Card 11 calls them Gentiles without ever making the link.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The question asks who the contribution is for. Two answers are people, but "Paul's journey on to Spain" is a thing, not a who, so it doesn't match the other answers.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: "Paul's not planning a trip, he's planning a whole season" doesn't click right away. A season of what? The image is unclear, and the joke falls flat.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: This blank only asks the baker to guess the wording of Romans 15:29, "fullness of the ___ of Christ." No story card sets it up, and nothing earlier lets the baker reason out "blessing" over "authority" or "suffering."

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "By sending him money for Spain" is close to something Paul really asks for in this passage. In Romans 15:24 he hopes the Romans will "equip me for my journey" to Spain, so a baker could argue for it.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.
